COURT’S OR JUDGE’S ORDERS
CLR No. 126 of 2025
Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Saurabh Kumar Pandey, learned 
counsel for the revisionist.
2. Mr. S.K. Mandal, learned counsel 
for the respondents.
3. In compliance of the previous order 
dated 13.11.2025, the revisionist paid a 
sum of Rs. 11,50,000/- towards arrear of 
rent to the respondent and for remaining 
arrear a month’s time he is praying.
4. A month’s time is granted to the 
revisionist to pay the remaining amount 
of arrear of rent. 
5. So far as restoration of the 
electricity is concerned, the learned 
counsel for the respondent/ landlord 
informed this Court that the 
respondent/landlord already submitted 
an application to the concerned 
electricity distribution division in this 
regard and he has no objection if the 
electricity connection is restored.
6. In such an eventuality, the 
concerned officer of the electricity 
distribution division is directed to restore 
the electricity forthwith subject to the 
payment of electricity due of the 
revisionist.
7. Let the record of the trial court 
record be summoned.
8. Put up this matter in the week 
commencing 9th March 2026.
9. Till then the revisionist shall not be 
evicted. It is made clear that if the  revisionist fails to pay the remaining 
balance amount towards arrear of rent, 
the respondent shall immediately move 
an application for vacation of the order.
(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.) 
05.01.2026
Parul

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
13.03.2026 CLR No.126 of 2025
Hon’ble Subhash Upadhyay, J.
1. Mr. Amar Murti Shukla, learned counsel for the 
revisionist.
2. Mr. S.K. Mandal, learned counsel for the 
respondents.
3. Perusal of order-sheet reveals that the learned 
counsel for the revisionist on 13.11.2025 had given 
an undertaking before the Coordinate Bench that the 
revisionist will clear entire arrears within 45 days, out 
of which, ₹ 20 lakhs will be paid by him within a 
month. 
4. In view of undertaking given by counsel for the 
revisionist, the Coordinate Bench, vide order dated 
13.11.2025, while granting interim order, had 
directed the revisionist to pay a sum of ₹ 10 lakhs 
within 15 days and the remaining amount within a 
month. Thereafter, the case was listed on 
05.01.2026, on which date, the Court recorded that 
in compliance of previous order, the revisionist has 
paid a sum of ₹ 11,50,000/- towards arrear of rent 
and, on the request of the revisionist, further one 
month’s time was granted to the revisionist to pay 
the remaining arrears. 
5. Learned counsel for the respondents submits 
that the revisionist has not paid the remaining arrears 
till today and as such the orders dated 13.11.2025 
and 05.01.2026 has not been complied with by him,
in totality.  6. Learned counsel for the revisionist submits that 
his client has met with an accident and, therefore, he 
could not pay the remaining amount, however, he 
undertakes to pay the same within a period of two 
weeks from today.
7. List this case on 27.03.2026.
8. Interim order dated 05.01.2026 is extended till 
the next date of listing. 
 (Subhash Upadhyay, J.) 
 13.03.2026
Rajni

COURT’S OR JUDGE’S ORDERS
CLR No. 126 of 2025 
Hon'ble Subhash Upadhyay, J.
1. Mr. Amar Murti Shukla and Mr. 
Saurabh Kumar Pandey, learned counsel for 
the revisionist. 
2. Mr. S.K.Mandal, learned counsel for 
the respondents. 
3. Vide order dated 13.11.2025, a 
Coordinate Bench of this Court noted the 
undertaking of learned counsel for the 
revisionist that the revisionist will clear the 
entire dues within 45 days, and within a 
month the revisionist will pay Rs. 20 lakhs. 
The revisionist was directed to pay a sum of 
Rs. 10 lakhs within 15 days of the date of 
passing of the order and the remaining 
amount was to be paid within a month. 
4. As per own case of the revisionist, till 
date only an amount of Rs. 18 lakhs has 
been paid to the respondent. Counsel for the 
respondent submits that the arrears were to 
be cleared within 45 days, however, till date 
even Rs. 20 lakhs has not been paid. Apart 
from that, the monthly rent from December, 
2025 has not been paid.
5. Learned counsel for the revisionist is  granted a week’s time to seek instructions 
from his client within which time, the 
arrears shall be cleared. 
6. In case, the said undertaking is not 
placed before the Court, the Court shall 
consider the stay vacation application filed 
by the respondent. 
7. List on 5th June, 2025. 
(Subhash Upadhyay, J.)
22-05-2026

COURT’S OR JUDGE’S ORDERS
CLR No. 126 of 2025
Hon'ble Subhash Upadhyay, J.
1. Mr. Amar Murti Shukla, learned counsel 
for the revisionist. 
2. Mr. S.K.Mandal, learned counsel for the 
respondents. 
3. Learned counsel for the respondents 
submits that the revisionist is in default of 
payment of monthly rent and till date the 
amount Rs. 22,78,000/- is due. This Court 
vide order dated 13.11.2025, had directed the 
revisionist to deposit a sum of Rs. 
20,00,000/- within a month. An undertaking
on behalf of the revisionist was also recorded
that he will clear the entire arrears within 45 
days.
4. The revisionist till date has only paid an 
amount of Rs. 20,00,000/-, which was to be 
paid within a period of one month from the 
date of passing of the order dated 13.11.2025. 
Thus, it is clear that there is no substantial 
compliance of the order dated 13.11.2025. 
The Coordinate Bench vide order dated 
05.01.2026, further observed that, in case, 
the revisionist fails to pay the remaining 
balance amount towards arrears of rent, the  respondent shall immediately move an 
application for vacation of the interim order. 
5. Learned counsel for the respondent 
submits that as compliance of the order dated 
13.11.2025 has not been made and arrears of 
rent has not been cleared, as such, the 
interim order is liable to be vacated.
6. This court finds substance in the 
arguments of learned counsel for the 
respondent, as the arrears of the rent has not 
been cleared as directed by the court on 
13.11.2025, as such, the interim order dated 
13.11.2025 is vacated. Stay Vacation 
Application (IA No. 2 of 2026) stands disposed 
of. 
7. List for hearing on 03.07.2026. 
(Subhash Upadhyay, J.)
 05.06.2026
Kaushal

4. An objection has been filed to the said stay

has been stated that till 15.07.2026, an 
outstanding amount of Rs.17,46,500/- is due

agreement that the rent payable to the

5. Learned counsel for the revisionist prays

the further sum of Rs.5,00,000/- towards the  outstanding dues. He shall also deposit the rent 
on or before 10th of every month. 
6. List on 07.08.2026. 
7. In the meantime, the revisionist may file 
the objections before the Executing Court, 
however till the next date of listing, the 
Executing Court shall not pass any final order.
